meanings: adjective: planned but not definite
examples: Nisha and her husband wanted to buy plane tickets for summer vacation, but they wisely did not while their schedules were still tentative.

meanings: verb: promise to do or start to do a large and difficult project
examples: After he'd gathered all the materials and tools, Steve was ready to undertake the construction of his new garage on his own, one piece at a time.

meanings: noun: a person who actively supports an idea
examples: Martin Luther King Jr. was a tireless advocate for the rights of African-Americans in the United States.

meanings: verb: to make two things be logical together
examples: Peggy was unable to reconcile her kind friend Jane with the murderous character Jane played on television.

meanings: verb: make someone do something
examples: Clara hoped her son would clean his room on his own, but eventually she had to compel him by threatening to take away his television.

meanings: noun: the force from moving
examples: A train moving at even the slowest speeds has enough momentum to make stopping difficult.

meanings: verb: win a victory over
examples: Determined to make more friends this year, Finn overcame his shyness and introduced himself to the new student.

meanings: noun: as a representative of somebody ("on [person]'s behalf" or "on behalf of [person]")
examples: After months of collecting money, the CEO was pleased to present a check to the charity on behalf of his company's employees.

meanings: verb: to force to move to another place
examples: The repeated floods in the capital city have displaced more than 10,000 people, many of whom are now living in their cars or on the streets.

meanings: verb: to cause to happen (usually a bad reaction)
examples: Darcy insulted Elizabeth's family repeatedly, hoping to provoke her into a fight.

meanings: noun: a small amount or individual used for studying the whole thing or group
examples: The scientist broke off a chip of the mysterious glowing rock and placed the specimen under the microscope to try to identify it.

meanings: noun: a small piece (usually left after most is gone)
examples: The dog waited patiently for the family to finish eating; he knew that his best chance for a scrap of hamburger came when they cleared the plates.

meanings: preposition: by going through or using
examples: The highway is full of traffic at this hour—it would be faster to travel via smaller streets.

meanings: noun: a danger
examples: The ice and rain made the road a hazard even to drivers who knew it well.

meanings: adjective: logical and understandable
examples: Sadly, the most popular politicians are rarely the ones with the most coherent arguments.

meanings: verb: to communicate information
examples: A skilled actor can convey complicated emotions simply through facial expressions and body language.

meanings: verb: to become too much to handle
examples: Jesse thought he could work two jobs while studying full-time, but his new schedule quickly overwhelmed him, and his grades soon dropped.

meanings: verb: to continue to exist although something/someone tries to stop it
examples: Mary began to fear she would fail and die while trying to swim across the English Channel, but she persisted and made it across.

meanings: adjective: having more than one possible meaning
examples: The coach told his team, "Move to that side of the field," but because he did not point, his directions were ambiguous, and nobody knew where to go.

meanings: noun: the time period of an important historical situation
examples: It is interesting to walk through a museum of eighteenth-century history, but few people would want to live in an era without electricity.

meanings: verb: to stay for longer than expected
examples: Although the invitation clearly stated that the party would end at midnight, there were a handful of guests still lingering at 2:00AM.

meanings: noun: a disadvantage, a negative part
examples: While the new office was cleaner and in a nicer part of town, the total lack of windows was a major drawback that changed the team's mind.

meanings: verb: to try to prevent; show opposition to
examples: The government's primary job should be to deter paths to war, not find reasons to start them.

meanings: verb: to try very hard to accomplish
examples: Ten-year-old Timmy fell down a lot while he was endeavoring to ride an adult's bicycle, but he eventually succeeded.

meanings: adjective: not where it is expected, missing
examples: Little Amy smiled up at me, her tongue poking through the hole formed by her absent front teeth.

meanings: noun: a system made of levels of power
examples: Chickens in groups form a hierarchy known as a "pecking order," which allows the stronger birds to eat first and have first choice of mates.

meanings: verb: to improve or make complete by pairing well
examples: Cecilia is an expert cook, especially when matching flavors—she always knows the perfect appetizer to complement any dish.

meanings: adverb: without much difficulty or delay
examples: Because Derek adored the famous scientist, he readily agreed to work for her without being paid.

meanings: adjective: complicated and difficult to understand
examples: Instead of solving the math problem in three simple steps, Kumar used a convoluted solution requiring fifteen steps.

meanings: adjective: very little, not enough
examples: When gasoline was expensive and scarce, people found ways to travel without using their cars.

meanings: adjective: not made correctly and not working
examples: Joan took her car back to the dealer who had sold it to her, asking that lock be repaired for free since it never worked and was clearly defective.

meanings: adjective: as a decoration
examples: When Harry tried to eat an apple in the lobby of a well decorated hotel, he was surprised to find it was made of wax—the fruit was ornamental!

meanings: verb: to officially order a new rule, tax, or punishment
examples: We'll soon find out what punishment will be imposed in response to the test results showing the football player used performance-enhancing drugs.

meanings: adjective: continuing forever without pause
examples: Although a perpetual motion machine would be an amazing source of energy, such things do not exist; everything comes to a stop at some point.

meanings: noun: a sudden loss of power or success
examples: An inability to match the lower prices of its competitors led to the company's downfall.

meanings: adjective: beautiful, graceful
examples: The carefully practiced, elegant movements of the ballet followed the beautiful sounds of the orchestra.

meanings: adjective: very well known and respected as high quality
examples: The Olympic Games are possibly the most prestigious athletic competitions in the world.

meanings: verb: to leave one area to live in another
examples: The winters felt longer and longer every year, until eventually John and Louise decided to migrate south to a warmer region.

meanings: verb: to give permission
examples: The young student dreamed of studying abroad, but her parents would not consent to her leaving for a foreign country.

meanings: verb: to send out into the air (used for light, sound, smell, etc.)
examples: The single lighthouse shone into the dark, emitting pulses of light that could be seen for miles.

meanings: verb: to acknowledge defeat
examples: I concede. You win!

meanings: verb: to make happy or satisfied
examples: Mrs. Iyer was not expecting her children to come visit her for Mother's Day, so she was extremely gratified when they did.

meanings: verb: to reach the highest or most developed point
examples: Beethoven's musical genius culminated in the 9th Symphony, which many consider his greatest work.

meanings: verb: to help the growth of something
examples: A good teacher not only teaches students how to do well on tests; a good teacher fosters curiosity and excitement to learn in her students.

meanings: verb: to come together into a larger number or amount over time
examples: Greg didn't receive much mail each day, but when he went on vacation for three weeks, it accumulated into a mountain of paper at his home.

meanings: adjective: thin and attractive
examples: The slender movie star told everyone that she worked out a lot to keep fit, but she actually just had a fast metabolism.

meanings: adjective: not easy or impossible to bend
examples: Tetanus toxin is famous for its ability to stop victims from moving and for the strained, tense, and rigid look of their muscles.

meanings: noun: a small amount of color
examples: To prevent his famous passengers from being seen by the public, the driver applied a heavy tint to his car's windows.

meanings: noun: a strong disagreement among many people
examples: Laws on gun control in the U.S. have caused controversy for many years.

meanings: noun: something that limits or restricts
examples: We don't have many resources, so we'll have to work with some very tight constraints.
